ai.description: *Kaestlea bilineata* is a small skink reaching 5 cm SVL. It is olive-brown with two distinct pale dorsolateral stripes and a dark mid-dorsal band. It features a translucent window in the lower eyelid.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Kaestlea bilineata* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous pale dorsolateral stripe on each side of the body, bordered by dark brown bands.
ai.habitat: *Kaestlea bilineata* inhabits leaf litter and rocky areas within high-altitude montane evergreen forests and shola grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically above 1,500m.
ai.behavior: The Two-lined Ground Skink is primarily diurnal, actively foraging through leaf litter for small invertebrates while relying on its speed to escape predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Kaestlea bilineata* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Kaestlea bilineata* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the high-elevation montane grasslands and shola forests of Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
